section_1.title: Introduction & Prerequisite Visuals
section_1.content: Define the problem: Given any simple closed curve (like a distorted circle), can we always find four points on it that form a square? Introduce the concept of a 'Configuration Space'—viewing the curve as a set of points in 2D space.
section_1.example: Visualize a messy loop of string on a table. The goal is to place a square stencil on top so all four corners touch the string.

section_2.title: Mapping the Geometry to Topology
section_2.content: Introduce the auxiliary function: Define a square by its center (x, y) and its side length s. Map the relationship between the points on the curve and the symmetry of the square. Use the concept of 'Intermediate Value Theorem' as a prerequisite to show that as we rotate the square, the 'errors' in corner placement must pass through zero.
section_2.example: Think of a 'robotic hand' trying to fit its 4 fingers onto the curve. If we rotate the hand, the distance between fingers changes continuously.

section_3.title: The Symmetry Argument
section_3.content: Explain the role of the Mobius strip or higher-dimensional topological spaces. Show that the set of all possible inscribed rectangles (where the ratio of sides is not necessarily 1:1) forms a surface where a solution is guaranteed. Narrowing this to a square requires identifying the specific 'diagonal' where length equals width.
section_3.example: A visual animation showing a rectangle morphing into a square as it slides and rotates along the boundary of the curve.

section_4.title: Application & Conclusion
section_4.content: Discuss the 'Square Peg Problem' status. While solved for smooth curves, it remains an active area of research for non-smooth curves. Summarize that topology proves existence even when we cannot calculate the exact coordinates.
section_4.example: Imagine a digital character trying to park a square vehicle perfectly against a curved wall; the math guarantees a 'perfect fit' exists, even if the driver can't find it easily.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Right side layout: x moves from ~1 to 6, y from ~2.5 to -2.5
                x = 2.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Inscribed rectangles form a continuous surface.", 
                         "A solution is guaranteed topologically.", 
                         "Identify the diagonal where length equals width."]
        self.setup_layout("The Symmetry Argument", lecture_lines)
        
        # Visual Elements

        self.place_in_area(curve, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Rectangle/Square representation
        rect = Polygon([-0.5, -0.3, 0], [0.5, -0.3, 0], [0.5, 0.3, 0], [-0.5, 0.3, 0], color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(rect, 'C3')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(curve), FadeIn(rect))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#ADFF2F"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(rect.animate.scale(0.8).set_color(ORANGE)) # Morphing
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#ADFF2F"))

        self.add(diag)
        self.play(Create(diag))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        self.wait(2)
